title: The Chemical Inventory of the Planet-hosting Disk PDS 70
question: What is the chemical inventory of the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk (detections, radial profiles, column densities, deuteration and N fractionation, C/O) and what does it imply for the gas accreted by the two planets?

data.bands: Band 6 (new data, program 2019.1.01619.S); Band 7 (archival, HCO+ 4-3 and 12CO 3-2)
data.arrays: array type not stated; 43-46 antennas after flagging per execution block (Table 1)
data.sensitivity: ~1 mJy/beam in a 1 km/s channel at ~0.4''-0.5''

what.value: Disk geometry and kinematics: M_star = 0.875 Msun, i = 51.7 deg, PA = 160.4 deg

evidence.quote: We use the following geometrical parameters: M$_{\rm star}=0.875\,M_\odot$, $i=51.7^\circ$, PA$=160.4^\circ$ (cite: keppler19).

what.value: Elevated emission surface z(r)=0.33 (r/1'')^0.76 for 12CO and HCO+

evidence.quote: using the best fit parameters by (cite: keppler19): $z(r)[\ensuremath{''}]=0.33\times(r / 1\ensuremath{''})^{0.76}$
with the systemic velocity being $5505\pm2\,$m s$^{-1}$ (cite: keppler19)

what.value: Initial parameters for the visibility-plane ring fit taken from the Band 7 continuum fit

evidence.quote: with the parameters initialized from the fit to the ALMA Band 7 continuum reported in (cite: keppler19)

what.value: 0.85 mm flux density 177 mJy (re-analysed with flux offset correction)

evidence.quote: By using their estimated flux density of 177 mJy, we obtain a spectral index of $2.49\pm0.44$ and $2.84\pm0.59$ in the 0.85-1.33 and 0.85-1.19 mm range.

what.value: SMA 1.33 mm flux density ~38 mJy as published; 63 mJy after recalibration (private communication)

evidence.quote: While they report a flux density of $\sim38$ mJy, a new calibration of the data leads to a flux density of 63 mJy for baselines $<15\,$k$\lambda$ (Mark Gurwell, private communication).

what.value: 12C/13C = 68 +/- 15 used to convert H13CN to HCN

evidence.quote: In order to derive HCN column densities, a $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 68$\pm15$ is assumed (cite: milam2005).

what.value: Molecular data (E_u, A_ul, g_u, partition functions) from CDMS

evidence.quote: taken from the CDMS catalogue (cite: cdms), and interpolate the partition function, $Q$, with a cubic spline.

what.value: PDS 70c semi-major axis 33.2 au (used to define the high-velocity channels inside the planet orbit)

evidence.quote: From (cite: wang_ea_2021), planet c has an orbit with semi-major axis of 33.2 au.

what.value: Model N(CS)/N(SO) ~0.03 for solar C/O; ~10 for C/O ~1

evidence.quote: Their reference model produces a disk averaged column density ratio $N$(CS)/$N$(SO)$\sim0.03$, while observations indicate a ratio with a lower limit $>1$.
A C/O ratio of $\sim1$ leads to a $N$(CS)/$N$(SO) ratio of $\sim10$ (cite: semenov_ea_2018).

what.value: C2H/13CO flux-ratio criterion: C/O>1 required when C2H 3-2 F=4-3 to 13CO 2-1 ratio >~0.2

evidence.quote: they showed that C/O$>1$ is required when the ratio of the C$_2$H $N$=3-2 $J$=$\frac{7}{2}$-$\frac{5}{2}$ $F$=4-3 line to the $^{13}$CO $J$=2-1 line is $\gtrsim 0.2$.

what.value: Thermochemical models: high C2H flux cannot be obtained with solar C/O; C/O ~1.5 required

evidence.quote: In the thermo-chemical models by (cite: miotello_ea_2019), such a high flux cannot be obtained with a solar C/O ratio, and elemental ratios close to $\sim1.5$ are required.

recipe.method: Per-EB continuum imaging showed pointing offsets; ring fitted in the visibility plane per EB, then phase centres shifted with fixvis and EBs re-aligned with fixplanet
key_parameters: 60 walkers, 2000 steps after burn-in
baselines <650 klambda used in the fit
phase-centre shift with fixvis, alignment with fixplanet
assumptions: outer ring modelled as a Gaussian ring because no inner disk is detected in single EBs

recipe.method: Spectral index of the flux calibrator from Band 3 and Band 7 used to correct Band 6 flux; offsets between EBs of the same setup corrected relative to the EB closest in time to the Band 7 calibrator measurement, following DSHARP, with gaincal
assumptions: Band 7 calibrator measurement was 8-18 days from the science observations

recipe.method: EBs of the same setup combined with concat; self-cal on the two setups separately: 3 rounds of phase self-cal and one amplitude round, applied afterwards to the unflagged, unaveraged visibilities
key_parameters: channels within +/-20 km/s of listed lines flagged before self-cal
continuum averaged with channels <500 MHz
model imaged down to 5 sigma of initial data, Briggs robust 0.5, elliptical mask; rms in annulus 2.55''-4.25''

recipe.goal: Image the continuum and derive flux densities and spectral index
recipe.method: tclean multiscale continuum images with robust=2 for flux density, superuniform weighting for high resolution; spectral index vs 0.85 mm flux; inner-disk upper limit from the cavity-centre intensity
key_parameters: flux density measured within the self-cal mask
assumptions: 0.85 mm flux density of 177 mJy from Isella+2019 and 10% absolute flux uncertainty in all datasets

recipe.method: uvcontsub first-order continuum subtraction; tclean multiscale with Keplerian masks; lines imaged -6 to +17 km/s with natural and robust 0 weighting, final per-line choice in Table 2; elevated emission surface for 12CO and HCO+
key_parameters: Keplerian mask geometry from Keppler+2019: M_star 0.875 Msun, i 51.7 deg, PA 160.4 deg
elevated surface z(r)=0.33 x (r/1'')^0.76 for 12CO and HCO+
weak lines c-C3H2 3_21-2_12 and H2CO 3_21-2_20 additionally uv-tapered by 0.7''
assumptions: line emission follows the Keplerian model fitted to 12CO 3-2

recipe.goal: Stack spectra and measure line fluxes and detections
recipe.method: Deproject and shift local spectra to systemic velocity with GoFish using the Keppler+2019 Keplerian fit, integrate within 3'' (4'' for 12CO 2-1), integrate spectrum over velocity windows; C2H F=4-3 and F=3-2 blend fitted with a double Gaussian; weak lines checked by azimuthally averaged spectra and a VISIBLE matched filter
key_parameters: integration window 3-8 km/s (default); 1.5-9.5 km/s for the two 12CO and HCO+; 2-9 km/s for 13CO, H13CN and C2H
flux uncertainty from standard deviation of unused velocity bins times sqrt(number of integrated bins)
C2H J=5/2-3/2 only half covered: only the part of the disk within 80 deg of the red-shifted major axis is used, azimuthal symmetry assumed
assumptions: Keplerian kinematics from Keppler+2019 apply to all lines

recipe.goal: Make integrated intensity maps and radial profiles
recipe.method: Integrated intensity maps over whole cubes with 2.5 sigma clipping and Keplerian masking; azimuthal average of deprojected moment-0 maps in annuli of 1/4 beam major axis
key_parameters: annulus width = 1/4 of the beam major axis
error bars: standard deviation within annuli divided by sqrt of number of independent beams

recipe.goal: Derive column densities, optical depths and H2CO excitation temperature
recipe.method: Optically thin column density with optical-depth correction, LTE; H2CO N and Tex fitted jointly from two transitions per 0.1'' annulus; other molecules fitted at fixed Tex of 20, 30, 50 K with tau<1 prior; c-C3H2, SO, CH3OH disk-averaged (upper limits from 3 sigma flux limits)
key_parameters: H2CO: 128 walkers, 1000 burn-in steps, 500 sampling steps per radial bin
C2H: Tex fixed to 20, 30, 50 K; 128 walkers, 1000 burn-in, 500 sampling steps
radial bins 0.1'' wide; c-C3H2 disk average uses a 3'' radius
C2H blended lines fitted with two Gaussians (scipy curve_fit), line centres fixed to the rest frequencies
assumptions: LTE, top-hat line profile for tau, partition function interpolated with cubic spline, CDMS molecular data

recipe.method: Column-density ratios of H13CN, DCN, HC15N (disk-averaged within 3'' and radial profiles), HCN = 68 x H13CN, Tex 30 K (20-50 K for uncertainty); cubes smoothed to a common 0.42'' beam
key_parameters: H13CN and HC15N compared in natural-weighted images; H13CN and DCN in robust=0 images
profiles limited to r <~ 1.8'' due to low snr
assumptions: uniform 12C/13C = 68 +/- 15 and equal Tex for the three isotopologues

recipe.goal: Infer C/O from C2H and CS/SO
recipe.method: Compare C2H flux and C2H/13CO ratio with thermochemical models (Miotello+2019, Fedele & Favre 2020) and the lower limit on N(CS)/N(SO) with Semenov+2018
assumptions: literature model grids (not tailored to a large cavity) apply qualitatively

recipe.goal: Compare radial peak locations with continuum and scattered light
recipe.method: Radius of peak integrated intensity (r>0.2'' for 12CO and HCO+) read from radial profiles without smoothing or fitting, error = 1/4 beam major axis; compared with 855 micron continuum and J-band polarized intensity

score_reason: Project codes and many processing parameters (self-cal intervals, robust values, weighting per line, integration windows, Tex grid, emcee set-up) are given and results are numeric, but cell/image sizes, masks, line-free channels, flux factors and priors are missing and several numbers are inconsistent between text and tables.
rediscovery_reason: Band 6 data from a single program (2019.1.01619.S) are expected to be archive-public, the line-flux and column-density recipe is largely given and results are numeric, though several imaging details would need to be inferred.
